title: IMProVE: a pilot study of prostate cancer screening in Yorkshire
official: Prostate cancer screening using a risk adapted PSA/image-based approach: pilot study for a Yorkshire-wide comparison with standard care
summary:
Background and study aims
In the UK, prostate cancer is the second commonest cause of cancer death in men and people with prostates. There is no NHS screening (searching for cancer in those without symptoms) for this cancer. Men considered at risk are offered a prostate specific antigen (PSA) blood test. However, this test is not definitive. Not all patients with prostate cancer have elevated PSA levels and high PSA values may be due to other causes. Screening for prostate cancer using PSA tests improves survival from the cancer but often finds slow growing cancers that do not need treatment. An MRI scan can identify which men have aggressive prostate cancer and which do not but is unaffordable for everyone. Evidence suggests that combining PSA testing with prostate MRI may improve the detection of aggressive prostate cancer while reducing unnecessary diagnosis of slow-growing cancers. This approach should reduce unnecessary detection of people with slow growing cancers, whilst saving many lives. Importantly, our approach is deliverable by the NHS. Before starting a larger trial, which might involve 300,000 people with a prostate, it is necessary to undertake a pilot study to test the study designs and ideas.

Firstly, the pilot will understand views of men from Black and from lower income backgrounds on prostate screening. Secondly, image-based testing will be compared with traditional NHS care in 4,500 people with a prostate. This study will find out how best to invite people who would benefit most. Thirdly, it will work out the most affordable way to screen for this cancer within the NHS.

Who can participate?
Men, or people with a prostate aged 50-69 years (inclusive) who are living at an address in selected locations within Leeds and Sheffield will be invited to take part. People who match the study criteria could also take part by signing up through our study website.

What does the study involve?
Taking part in the study may involve: 
1.	Clinic appointment for a Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA) blood test: about 30-45 minutes 
2.	Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan or biopsy (if needed): separate appointments, about 1 hour each 
3.	Surveys: short online questionnaires completed at several time points over 12 months

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Possible benefits:
Participants may not benefit directly however their participation will help improve how prostate cancer is detected in the future.

Possible risks:
Participants may need extra tests or appointments. Waiting for results may feel worrying for some people. Some cancers found may not have caused harm (overdiagnosis).

Where is the study run from?
The University of Sheffield is the sponsor. The Cancer Prevention Trials Unit at Queen Mary University of London is coordinating the study. The Coordinating Investigator is Professor James Catto, Consultant Urological Surgeon, University of Sheffield. The study team are also working with Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
April 2027 to June 2028.

Who is funding the study?
Yorkshire Cancer Research, UK.

Who is the main contact?
IMProVE study team at improve@qmul.ac.uk.

interventions.name:
Participants will be invited to take part in prostate cancer screening as part of the IMProVE study via 1 of 5 invitation routes, selected at random:
1.	SMS invitation only
2.	SMS invitation + SMS reminder
3.	SMS invitation + letter reminder
4.	Letter invitation + SMS reminder
5.	Letter invitation o

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Capacity to provide informed consent prior to study entry
2. Men,or people with a prostate aged 50 – 69 years (inclusive) at the time of invitation into the study 
3. Living at an address in selected locations within Leeds and Sheffield. 
4. Have a phone number*
5. Have an NHS number
5. Residency in the UK for 12 months prior to consent to enter the study

*Participants recruited via NHS DigiTrials will require a mobile telephone number to receive the SMS study invitation.
Exclusion criteria:
1. PSA testing within 12 months prior to invitation into the study
2. Prostate MRI scan within 24 months prior to invitation into the study
3. Prostate biopsy within 36 months prior to invitation into the study
4.Received antibiotics for urinary tract infection within 3 months prior to receiving invitation to the study
5. Current or prior prostate cancer diagnosis
6. Participant has opted out of data use via the National Data Opt-Out or Study Specific Opt-Out
7. A weight ≥ 200kg
8. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≥ 2 due to a severe comorbidity*
9. Known chronic kidney disease with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR – based on the CKD-EPI Equation) of ≤30 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD stage 4–5), receiving renal replacement therapy including dialysis, or previous kidney transplantation** 

*NB – This will be self-reported by participants against the following lay wording “A severe medical condition which means you have difficulty carrying out normal daily activities e.g. able to care for yourself but unable to work or carry out strenuous activities.” 

**NB – This will be self-reported by participants against the following lay wording “Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have severe kidney disease or kidney failure, or are you currently under hospital care for kidney failure or disease (for example, seeing a kidney specialist, receiving dialysis, or having had a kidney transplant)?”
